utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, sir. Good morning to everyone. I see that all the accused are here, Defence teams are in full force except for Mr. Bourgon. Prosecution like yesterday, Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye. The witness is already present in the courtroom. Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome back. We are resuming the examination in chief, and then I pass you on to the various Defence teams for their cross-examination. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, counsel, ladies and gentlemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think when we left off yesterday was very near the end, if not the end of examining the witness in relation to the map that was introduced as an exhibit. I would just have a few questions I'd like to pose to the witness in order to complete the direct examination. Good morning, Witness. You had indicated yesterday that you have a fairly thorough familiarity with these electronic -- the electronic versions of the intercepts that were processed by your unit. In relation to that, I would like to ask you, could you tell us if there is specific information that is required to be placed on the electronic version of the intercept when it's sent to the headquarters in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may not have understood your question fully, but I will try to answer it. Only the recording that have been listened in to are placed in the electronic version and sent to the command. We did not detract anything from it or add to it. That was the main rule. We did not go into the contents of the conversation as to who the persons in fact were. We were merely interested in the contents of the conversation, and I had to take an oath that I would abide by these rules and whatever we heard is what is contained in the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Other than the text, these printouts that were transmitted to the headquarters of the 2nd Corps, do they contain other information such as the site from which the transmission had been sent from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each heading of the document, or the report, clearly stated which connection this was, the frequency, the direction it came from, the numerical code, the channel, and the designation for this route that we chose. It was either 624 or 625, depending on the route of the connection. Our task was to forward the documents as they were to the command. In addition to written information, every week, at the end of each shift, we took over fully taped recordings that would then -- those ones that had been used would be erased, and we would take the erased blank tapes back with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could I have, if I may, I think it's been marked for identification, P02312, displayed for the witness? Thank you. Can you see that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I just want to refer you to the header, the top part of this document, and I wondered if you could just take us through the various demarcations on there, such as the site, the date, things like that, and let the Court know exactly what those are or how they are designated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to be as clear as possible. This is the classic heading. The first line says, "Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Since we had a direct connection with the command of the 2nd Corps, in fact what you see in the second line is the 2nd Corps command. The third line says that it's the radio relay, surveillance station, the location in the north. The fourth line is the reference number of the document that was sent as the first document on that date, because we see it says 01/14795. So that's the first report to leave this facility on the 14th of July 1995. The reference number is, of course, 01; and then the number after the slash is in fact the date. We thought this would be the simplest way of designating these or referencing these documents; and then the last line bears the date, 14th of July 1995. We had a certain code designated for every day at the KZ, and it was under that code that all the documents on that date would be sent. On the following day, we would have a different code; and, as I said, we received these codes from Sarajevo every month. The classic daily report would be sent by the unit charged with doing this job. We see below what is typical of this. Every person manning this particular post had the obligation to write down the frequency the conversation was heard; and there you have it, 785.000 megahertz, and that's the frequency on which the conversation was picked up. Then the "CH" abbreviation stands for channels. This is the third channel on the route, and I will try to explain this. In the communications system, a certain chain of command would be given a given channel. There were channels that were clearer, that had less noise in them. The channels between channel 3 and channel 5 were reserved for commanding structures, for officers, and we can see that this was picked up on channel 3. At the time of intercept-- of the intercept is 0704 and the route is southeast, and that's from the facility from which the intercept was picked up. And this was used in the event that the persons taking part in the conversation do not state where they are calling from; or if they are not even calling from a facility we know, then we would designate them as X, Y participants because they are unknown. And then we have the text of the intercept as it was taped. In the lower right-hand corner, we have abbreviations which are -- these are the initials of the persons producing the report. The first initials on the left is the initials of the person who typed the report, encrypted it and sent it to Tuzla, and the second pair of initials are the initials of the person picking up the conversation and noting it down. And this served us to know who took part in making these reports. The initials on the left-hand side would normally be the same for a week, because that would be the person designated to do the job for the week; whereas, the initials on the right-hand side could vary, because we had seven to eight people who would be picking up the conversations and noting them down, or rather, recording them and then noting them down. And it could have been any of those seven or eight persons at any given time doing that job.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. With respect to the report number on this particular exhibit, is that designated by the number 01?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the first report or conversation that was picked up that morning and sent to the command. We could send as many as 50 reports a day; however, on average we would send 20 to 30 of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So it's fair to say there was no fixed number of reports that was sent daily from your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The amount of reports and the work load did not depend on us. It depended on the persons involved in communication. If the air waves were busy that was normal, because it reflected the situation on the ground; but if the situation was stable or calm, then there would be less -- there would be less conversations in the air waves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the time of the given intercept, you've indicated that the times are designated particularly on this document as an example as 0704 and 0750, but there are no dates that are indicated there. Is the proper way to read this document -- is the proper way to read the document such that those intercepts that are recorded underneath that heading can be assumed to have been recorded on the date that's indicated on the report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a certain delay, because it took some time for the report to take its formal shape. First, the conversation had to be recorded, then it had to be noted down into the notebooks, then it had been to be taken to the KZ operator to be typed up and to be given a number. The time contained here is the time when the intercept was recorded or heard. There was a book on the KZ -- in the KZ department, which stated the date or the time, when the report was sent over so that the KZ operators up at Tuzla could have a clear list of the reports received and sent. There could not have been any mistakes done, because the system was well coordinated. But let me just note that the reports that were received just before midnight, for instance, if a conversation was recorded at 2300 hours or 2330 hours, then the report might actually have been sent the -- on the following day and the code would change. So they would not be sent on the same day they were recorded. But this only happened with the intercepts that were recorded just before midnight. However, if the information was urgent and could not be subject to this delay, then we would communicate the intercept over the phone. Otherwise, we would take the normal procedure of taking -- of sending the reports to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With respect to the report that is were recorded just close to midnight or the turning of the hour of the day, would they appear in the following days report as the first report of that day with a relatively high hour designation such as 2200 or 2300 hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The time when the intercept was recorded was clearly stated, as let's say 2300 hours, and then it would be sent on the following day. Let me say that this took place rarely but it, nevertheless, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you would just bear with me for one moment, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Zivanovic is going first. Mr. Zivanovic is appearing for Mr. Popovic in this case, yes, Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agreed with my colleague Zivanovic to go first, because I have some commitments later on. I believe all my colleagues are aware of this and have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Zivanovic was about to tell us precisely that. So Mr. Sarapa, you go first, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent. I did not want to just barge in with the first question like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you tell me which military school you completed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I completed the military high school and specialised in communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: What sort of work experience did you have in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked at the surveillance centre, military post 1925 in Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: In the course of the war in the BiH, did you cooperate with the intelligence organs at the level of the corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had this professional line of cooperation. It wasn't a chain of command line, but it was quite natural.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Did you know which areas did the platoons from the divisions cover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, I did. The platoons for the most part covered the areas covered by the area, like the 21st division covered Posavina. The area of surveillance was always by 30 percent larger than the area of operation of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Can you tell us the platoon for electronic reconnaissance from the 24th and 25th division, which areas did they cover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th division covered from Zvornik to Sekovici and the 25th covered the area of Majevica --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please break between question and answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Stop, stop, stop. Again, we have the perennial problem when two persons engaged in a discussion or questions speak the same language. Both Mr. Sarapa and you, Witness, speak the same language or are speaking the same language. So you have a tendency to overlap and one doesn't allow the other one to finish before you butt in with your answer or Mr. Sarapa with his question. So please allow a very brief interval of time between question and answer; because, otherwise, the interpreters will find it very difficult to translate the entire -- what you're saying in its entirety. Yes, Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Did you cover the communications of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Did you cover the communications of the 28th Division in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what I know, we did not monitor the communications for the simple reason that the 28th Division did not have sophisticated equipment. As far as I know, they only had the one short wave station.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Tell me, did you cover the communications on ultra wave -- ultra short waves that were done by the Motorolas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had the possibility to do that. However, we did that to a lesser extent, because these were shorter distance communications. It was only if we used the repeater that we listened to such communications. It was units at the level of brigade and divisions that covered these communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know who Semso Muminovic is? Are you familiar with the name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I do know him. I believe this person came from Teocak or Sapna. He was a military man. I don't know what he's doing now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, again, I have to repeat, slow down and allow a pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the conversations between Semso Muminovic and the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Vinko --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last name, if you could repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Vinko, Mr. Sarapa, Vinko who? I would imagine it's Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't want to say it myself. So okay, we have it in the record now. We don't have to worry about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the 24th division?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Mr. Zivanovic, are you taking over or are you announcing that someone else will?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will take over, Your Honour. Your Honour, before my cross-examination, I would like to provide an explanation in relation with the use of exhibits and probably had with the previous witness. To explain to you, in the list of the exhibits that we are going to use in our cross-examination, we have included among others all the books of intercepts, because we did not know exactly which intercepts would be used in our cross-examination. So that only after the examination-in-chief, we wanted to decide which intercepts to use in our cross-examination. But now we have a technical problem, to wit, all these books amount to 2.000 pages, and they could not be put into the EDS system. Therefore, we had to produce those intercepts either through videolink or through or to put them on the ELMO. So this produced some delays in production of our exhibits. I should have done that during the examination of the previous witness. I apologise and I'm taking this opportunity now, and I believe that we will have no further problems of that kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you for giving us that information and also for the attitude you have adopted, Mr. Zivanovic. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, let's go into private session for a short while, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you forward the company reports deciphered to the command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you encode them again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that, among other things, that you performed an analysis of the reports received. Could you describe the way, the method that you used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the first analysis or primary analysis, standard procedure at the unit level. The main task and out come of that analysis is to extract maximum possible information about the organisation and the schematic of the communications of the VRS to detect which relay nodes, which commands, which units hide under certain code, which would enable us to perform further analysis also. Each day a piece of information or a certain person if a name of a son-in-law, son, daughter, wife, were referred to with respect to a certain person, we would open a database on that person and the information obtained through radio surveillance, which would make our further work easier. The softer side of the work in radio relay is that codes were changed very infrequently, maybe once or twice a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, how many men were involved in the maintenance of databases or records on the persons mentioned in the intercepted conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two people, and I as a third person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you did not perform a content analysis, you analysed just the frequencies and channels that you may find them again in the future?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already stated, we were not interested and we did not have the time to deal with facts or who had -- who said what or who gave which information. At that point, it was important for us to hear who said something, and that that original information is sent to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive information from platoons via the telegram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive information from the platoon over the telegram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An abbreviated version of such reports would come through that mode of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In which situations would reports be sent over the telegram?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In situations which required urgent response. For instance, the posulovo [phoen] at Ozren when they were active and they would shell Tuzla and some other places, and whenever they were doing something with their artillery, we would receive immediate and urgent reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Telegram communication was used because it was faster than the computer communication?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said we did not understand. We used the telegram form, but we used radio packet system of relaying information. So it is a radio communication, but we used the telegraphic form, just a single sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can we go ahead?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's redact lines 6 and 7, and go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were the telephone lines between those two facilities that I mentioned, did they function properly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time from the northern facility, we had two types of communication; (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted)- was a relay station which had optical visibility with the other two and an underground telephone link with the Dubrave airport.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment, Mr. Vanderpuye. Let's redact also lines 16, 17, please, 16, 17 and 18, up to "radio packet;" and even the next line, yes, and even the next line and line 20, up to"reasons." You're not being careful both of you, actually, in trying to avoid mentioning names. Otherwise, we will have to revert to private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to confront the witness with two reports. I'm not sure whether this should be done in private session. We are discussing direct intercepts. Is it technically possible for those -- for the content not to be shown or broadcast outside the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That is possible, yes. That is possible. The understanding is the following, with the technicians, please. We will see the document or exhibit on our screen. Unless you have specific authorisation from us to broadcast those images, then you're not to broadcast them. Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye, I apologise to you. I saw you standing, but I suppose you also had objection to retaining those four lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I supposed that was the reason. I forgot to ask you again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's Defence Exhibit 1D72.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw many such reports. I would like to focus your attention to the heading, not the content of the report. By the heading, I mean what can be visible above the line. You see the number of this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You see it's a Daily Report RI?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can see who it is addressed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like the witness to see another report, ERN number is 6644. It's not on e-court. I'm afraid that we are going to have to show it in this manner. 6694 is the page, the four last digits. I would like to focus your attention to the upper part of this page, of this report. I'm not going to delve into its contents. First of all, I have to tell you that this is not the same report as the one. Can you notice that there is no number designating this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you notice that this report has no addressee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the content of this stencil? First of all, who would put this rubber stamp here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is known to me. I will try to be as simple as possible in my explanation. Of course, there is no indication of any addressee because this report is the report received at Tuzla by the encrypter, and his duty was to place such a rectangular seal or stamp on it and give it to his boss.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the term "processed" in the third line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the moment when this report was deciphered and made available for use. Above it are the standard codes, and these codes were matched at the end of each business day, in terms of how many reports were sent and how many reports were received.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Whoever received this sort of a telegram, did they have to erase the addressee?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did so. I wasn't there to control their procedures, but generally I know the procedure. And you see that this document was just a report, not a radio surveillance report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether this report was sent by your unit or from a unit under your command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report, I believe, was sent from our unit, this specific one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell it by the heading?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you print texts of the reports that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reports were printed at two places, and this is the reason why this report was produced. They would be printed in the unit command, within the company at Par Selo. The other two facilities we could not print them. And the second place the reports would be printed out at would be the security organ, and this particular report was printed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Intelligence organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record the last document that Mr. Zivanovic made use of, the complete ERN number is 02046694. Thank you. Go ahead. And we have a break in about four minutes or three minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you send printed reports to your higher command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not permitted to transport the reports in a written or a printed form. Our obligation was to store them in binders; and as producers of such reports, we had the duty to save-keep them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you kept them safe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Deciphered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Ciphered as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody verify or check the accuracy of deciphering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is not very clear to me. Simply, people who were engaged at encryption were specially trained. The training was performed partly in Tuzla, partly in Sarajevo. The cryptographers took an oath. They were certified for their work; and from the state and military security organs, were licensed to perform their work. Those people were not mobilised and simply appointed among the conscripted. They had to follow certain procedure and be trained.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You would send the tapes to the units under your command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you would receive filled tapes interest them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given the distance between the two facilities, whenever shift would change, we would take erased blank tapes and take the full tapes and would take them to the 2nd Corps command. And I told you already that the largest problem we had, apart from paper, were the tapes, magnetic tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then these tapes would be copied to some other tapes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a team in that department who listened to the tapes, and they were the second filter. They decided which conversations were interesting; and on the basis of the material that they had available, they would copy some conversation to other tapes. They would erase the tapes at hand and send them back to the units for reuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe, Your Honour, this is the right time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zivanovic, we'll have a break. How much more time do you require for your cross-examination? You've been one hour already.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe some 45 minutes more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. As I indicated yesterday, 45 minutes, and I know the Court was kind with the last witness with me. I will try to cut it short to approximately half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Ms. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I believe I will fit within the announced 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll stick to my yesterday's estimation. I believe 20 to 25 minutes will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One hour, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Unlikely to have any cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Sarapa has done his cross-examination already. We have two hours and a half. We should try and make an effort to finish this witness. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, you will have all noticed that Judge Stole is back with us. So we will resume the sitting with the composition, with the full composition. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. We are just briefly we are in the process of trying to organise the exhibits that we would tender in relation to there witness's testimony, and there had been some discussion yesterday on, I guess, marking some exhibits for identification, for tender at a later time. They were intercept-related. We have other documents such as maps and photographs and chain of custody evidence that we are not entirely sure whether that should also be put off to a later time. We would appreciate the court's guidance in that respect, because--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put it like this: The only point we made, when the question of intercepts arose and the tendering into evidence, was that since intercepts generally, across the board, in other words, were being challenged by all the Defence teams, all intercepts for the time being will not be formally admitted until we have an opportunity -- we would have had an opportunity to go through all the relative evidence, and they will only be entered into the records temporarily and marked for identification purposes only. But that's as relates to the intercepts and to no other documents. All other documents we cannot advise you as to what to do, whether you wish to tender them now or whether you wish to tender them later. That's up to you, your choice, and we will not interfere with that. But I speak for myself for the time being and I stand to be corrected. I haven't heard as yet any objections brought forward to these other ancillary documents. Not the intercepts themselves. I'm referring to ancillary documents. If we receive objections, then obviously we will hear what the objection is and decide whether to admit them now or postpone that until a later point in time and have them marked for identification purposes as well like the intercepts. So that's the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your unit, among other things, you also stored tapes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: These were only the tapes that were sent to you from the higher command, or did they include also tapes sent to you from subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to explain this. We always had a given amount of tapes which did not even remotely meet our requirements, not even the 5 percent of what we needed. In late 1995, after the signing of the Dayton Accords, the army was restructured and the platoons of subordinate units became part of the whole structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've discussed this already, but I wanted to clarify something else. You had the tapes that you received from your subordinate units and which you later on forwarded to the higher command. The higher command partly copied these conversations on to other tapes and returned the erased tapes to you or returned the recorded tapes to you which you then reused. My question to you was: Did you use only the tapes that you received from your subordinate structures, or did you also use tapes that you received from the higher command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not keep the tapes in our unit. The higher command would take the tapes at the end of the shifts and take them to the other facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, these tapes did not stay with you for longer periods of time than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Zivanovic and witness, please, again, may I appeal to you to allow a short pause between question and answer. I can sense the stress in the interpreter's voice trying to catch up with both of you, when you overlap. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the witness please be shown Exhibit number -- that's the Prosecution Exhibit number 1075.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You signed this document, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No broadcast of this document on the air, please, unless we issue a counterorder. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the first column, which has the heading,"Title or Name?" Can you explain to me what this abbreviation stands for, STPOV, and the number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we didn't have the originals that were used for that purpose, we gave a reference number to each of the notebooks in order to make them retrievable. This designation means that the notebook was entered into a logbook under this number and with this date. We would enter 15 or 20 notebooks into the log and take them to these facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you would do this at the time when the notebooks were still empty, before they were filled up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of the document, can we please turn to page 5? It is at the very bottom of page 5. There, it reads, "Handed over by," then there is your name and signature; and on the right-hand side, "Taken over by," and then another name. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the handover of the notebooks and of the material was not done on that date. Can you tell us why do we have this written; who handed over and who received the documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, the list and the documents were an annex to the minutes, which clearly state the date when the transfer of documents took place. This is merely an annex to the minutes, and I was authorised by my superior to sign the list and I handed it over to the gentleman whose name we see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 1 of the document? Do you see the column which says "facility" or building? And you can see that it's empty. Can you tell me or explain to me what this means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since the notebooks were entered in chronological order, we left this column empty, because some of the notebooks were sent to the northern facility and some were sent to the southern facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at page 2 of the document? Under number 23, if you look at this row, under the column "building," there is this one word. Can you tell us what this means in the context of the minutes or the record?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fourth column states that the notebook did not contain any information as to when it was made available for use or when it was filled up. But we know which facility it came from; in this case, it came from the northern facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Numbers 26 and 27, the same thing applies to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In row number 22, we have the information as to when the notebook was made available for use, but not when it was filled up. Does it come from the same facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact of the matter is that probably the notebook was not filled up. It wasn't fully filled up, and that's why we have only the date when it was made available for use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to the notebooks being made available for use, which amount of notebooks would you normally send to a given facility and what did it depend upon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except for the chain of command and the receiving of reports from facilities, before one shift would end, we would normally receive requests from different persons concerning their needs. Commanders of these facilities would monitor the expenditure of supplies and would regularly notify their requests accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you keep a record of the notebooks you issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, in the second column, the notebooks were entered into the logbook kept at Par Selo. Of course, we kept a record, and we always went back to check which of the notebooks were sent back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that normally the shift that was leaving would take out the new notebooks and would then come back with the old, used up ones. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When a shift would be going out into the northern facility, say, how many notebooks would they take with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On average, a dozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how many would they come back with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of notebooks coming back would always be by 1 percent lower, because they always kept some for use.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The notebooks that would be taken over there, would they be circulated into use immediately? Would they be used immediately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the notebooks that they used up. As they used up a notebook, they would automatically take a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it possible for one notebook to be used even before an older one that was earlier in use was actually filled up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you, yourself, controlled and saw that the notebooks matched or whether they matched with the reports.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice that some of the notebooks lacked dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it happened. That's why we had shifts, and that's why we insisted on the adherence to the rules governing notebooks; but, of course, people committed mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let's say you had four intercepting posts on a given -- in a given facility, and let's say you had ten notebooks that were being used. Could mistakes take place there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not required, under the law, to keep the notebooks. The report that was typed up in the computer was given a date, and we did things this way because we had to be quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, if you wanted to double check a date, you could not do that by consulting the notebooks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would match the report that was typed up with the notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If the typed up report contains the date and the notebook does not, then you would not be able to see if the dates tallied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will be frank again. I did not pay particular attention to the dates. I looked at the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is a daily business, so you can understand why he was more bothered with the content, rather than the dates, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us why some of the notebooks - and you were able to see that for yourself - do not contain the dates of when they were first put to use and when they were closed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were either empty or halfway filled when they came out of use, or simply persons who used them forgot to put these dates on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Subsequently, these notebooks would end up in your hands to be double checked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the notebooks came back, they were all stored in a metal safe that was kept in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that the date was missing as to when the notebook was no longer used, could also mean that the notebook was only halfway filled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me. I did not pay particular attention to that, because the report that was typed up into the computer was the official document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: For some reason, we find quite interesting one of the dates, and that's the 15th of July. That's the focus of some of the events we've been dealing with in this case. Looking at this list of yours, I arrived at the conclusion that at the time, on this date, there were 12 notebooks in use, based on the information you have in this list; and if you want me to, I can also give the numbers of the notebooks, but would you agree that this is possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I will explain this quite -- in simple terms. I remember this quite clearly. We had ten-day shifts. One shift would change on the 4th, the other one on the 14th. And, of course, on the 15th, it would so happen that there were many notebooks open, because the air waves were quite busy and many reports had to be produce.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When I said 12 notebooks, I referred only to the notebooks that were entered into the records. The dates were there. We were able to see that the dates when they were made available for use were prior to the 15th, and they were still in use after the 15th. However, there are 15 more notebooks, according to this list, that were in circulation in this period of time, quite certainly, but we don't have a date of either when they were put to use or when they were closed, when they were no longer used. Is this possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Please, again, both of you - I'm not just referring to one or the other - both of you again you've fallen back to the practice of overlapping. So please go ahead, Witness. You can answer the question now. The question has been put. I think it's his turn to answer the question. All right. Is that all you need to answer? You have to answer. Okay. Then let's proceed to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at the notebook under number 111? That's page 4, I believe. Can you please read the date? There is the question mark, and in brackets it says, "torn off." What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, this means that someone had torn off a part of the cover page, and that's why we wrote it down this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to me the following? Number 112, for instance, and there are several such notebooks, where you don't have this reference number strictly confidential and the date.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever features could identify a notebook were written down on this list. In this case, this notebook was not entered into the record. There was no reference number. We only knew that the notebook said that it was RRU-1. And we wrote that it was an A 4 format notebook, a large notebook; and in the last column, we wrote the dates of when it was first used and last used.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, because item 111 is not on page 4, as we have in line 3 of the transcript. It's page 4 to 5, but on page 5 of the document. Also while we are at this, you used the word which was translated to us as torn off, and the witness agreed with that. Could we have an indication, at least for our purposes, of which is the relative word. Is it the one in brackets [B/C/S spoken], or which is the word that would be translated into English as "torn off"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would mean that this part, which contained the date, was torn off from the page. That's what I -- that's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have not understood me. I just want to hear the word in the -- the relative word, corresponding word, in B/C/S, pronounced by one of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The word is [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see on page 1 - and I believe that it can be scrolled down - under 5, you also have a notebook without the strictly confidential mark, and under number 8. And we can scroll up to see more such examples. Can we scroll up or scroll down, rather? Under 11, under 14, there is a number of such rows, 16, 17, 18, 19. You can see for yourself. So there are many notebooks that have not been recorded and marked with the strictly confidential remark.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain, although I'm not quite sure. There is a possibility that some of these notebooks originated from the 21st Division. There is a possibility that these notebooks came from the 21st Division; and that material, when we handed it over, was in a heap. We had to work very quickly. And we just jotted down the basic elements that were on the notebook, and we record them as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are fully right, because if we -- if you want, we can count them. There are 47 such notebooks which do not bear the strictly confidential mark, but only ten come from the 21st Division. And we can see under number 20 is one such notebook, if we could go to that spot on the page. Number 20, if it's possible, yes. We can see it now. It says, "RRU-1, 21st Division." So out of 47 notebooks, ten come from the 21st Division, and the other 37 originated from your unit. Can you agree with me - and I've been perusing this overview - that 135 notebooks were delivered on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that 135 documents were handed over. Out of that number of 135, 134 were notebooks. And the number 135 was a heap of papers, which was put together to resemble a notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. If you take a look at all these documents, you will see that out of the documents and pertaining to the relevant period under our scrutiny that only six notebooks have all the required elements, have this strictly confidential remark, and the date of opening and the date of closing. All others lack at least one of these elements.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whenever coming to my duty at the unit, one of my tasks was to perform my -- to make my men more military-like. Many of them were civilians, and they were -- had to be instilled with some security mindedness and some military discipline. Otherwise, I will agree with what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you take a look at notebook number 3 -- under ordinal number 3. You see that it was recorded as at 13 of May, but it was put to use a day earlier. How can you explain this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it was a mistake in recording. It was done by the officer of the company, and he simply made a mistake as to the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. On the 24th of April 1998, you were there when this documentation was handed over to representatives of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this document? If you wish, you can be shown it. That is from the Prosecutor's list, document number 1068.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's decide whether we are going to show it to him or not, because otherwise we will be wasting time. Do you want the witness to see this document or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the witness whether he wishes to be shown it. As far as I'm concerned, it is not necessary for me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you explain what it's all about?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it would be best for the witness to see the document. The document 1068.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's a report from the handing over of these materials to the Tribunal's representatives. You can see it for yourself. Did you draft this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did somebody dictate the content, or did you draft it yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, my superior officer ordered me to draft this document, and he signed. I was just the typist.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that these documents were handed over as per a written order of the commander of the division, I mean, commander of the corps. It's stated somewhat lower in the document, if we could scroll down, please. There is this statement in the last paragraph. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You handed this documentation to Stephanie Frease, as an ICTY representative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see that you did not seek any documents, ID documents, from her to confirm her identity and capacity of ICTY representation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that was done was done by -- with the superior officers. Of course, they must have performed these formalities with the corps commander or Chief of Staff; and since these concerned the documents, I just typed the document and drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This would be the same what you did when you made a list of documents with the ICTY representative Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, on the next day, you handed over certain tapes. Do you know why these tapes were not handed over on the same date, on the 24th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason -- there was no reason which would concern us. The person representing the Tribunal had some other tasks on the ground. He packed everything into a box. He went somewhere else and returned the next day to take the documents. We both signed our names across that box.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me when that person selected the tapes, he, with you, did not or did you listen to the tapes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not listen to the tapes. We listened to just a small portion, because the tapes had some stickers indicating roughly what was recorded on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us take a look at Prosecution document 1069. This is a report on the handing over or handover of these tapes. Can we scroll down, please, the text? You drafted this document as well on the basis of what your superior officer dictated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read the penultimate paragraph of this text? And could you tell me that apart from writing down, "Hunter, Jack, US Army, and social security number," how did you know this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that because the gentleman introduced himself civilly to us, and he gave us this document, this ID document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he purport at the same time to be an ICTY representative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did say that, and his task at the time was to establish and determine whether it was possible from the locations that we used to overhear and survey the -- and intercept such conversations. I believe that he was an electronic surveillance expert from the US.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see that you had no reservations towards Ms. Frees and Mr. Nicholls on the previous occasion, but how come that you sought that he proves his identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. He did it on his own volition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, you're not allowing a pause between question and answer, please. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do not doubt that he showed you the ID, but this is -- what is unclear is that you did not have to do that and write it in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman demanded that we do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was done on his -- at his request?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the reason for that was that he left the documents with us and had to take them the next day, I mean the tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But he did take them on that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the tapes were packed and packaged together. Previously, they were put in a warehouse; and as I stated, this gentleman and I signed the box, and he had some other obligations out on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this is why he produced an ID document to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As the text continues, in the next paragraph -- in the same paragraph, there is the following piece of information: "Together with an obligation that in the intelligence and security department, to listen, select the tape, and to resolve the issue of further use and return." Did your superior officer demand that such a clause be included?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Superior officers, it is stated in the last paragraph, state that there should have been a prior approval from the Department for Intelligence and Security for any handing over of such sensitive material. And it's stated in the lower left-hand corner, one copy of this document was sent to our superiors in Sarajevo, because orders came to us from Sarajevo down the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that these tapes were much more important than the notebooks that you handed over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, when the ICTY representatives came, initially we did not know what was of their interest; and only as we worked and as we went along, we concluded that there might be some additional material that could be useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as we are discussing, the last paragraph, could you tell us, as I see, there is an important difference between the handing over of this document and the previous documents, as per the previous material you had written, "Order of the corps commander." But here in this case, you have another name and an indication that he's a member of the intelligence and security department. What does this mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, it went for the person who was in charge of counter-intelligence and security, and he was my superior in terms of security; and since we had to do this quickly, my boss contacted this person and sought approval for the handover. We stated this as a per standard operating procedure, where you have both oral and written orders. And it is stated here that that person issued an oral order and approval for the materials to be handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But this was not sought from the assistant commander for security intelligence or head, chief of -- chief of intelligence and security department, as in the case of the first batch of documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This depends on what was put in the report. I personally know that the procedure would be either that or an alternative. So certain persons would carry out orders given by their superior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I see that this approval was delivered over the phone. So it wasn't in writing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now take a look at the report from the 10th of May 1999. That's Exhibit -- Prosecution Exhibit 1071. As you can see, under 1, it is stated that original transcripts of intercepts are handed over in original notebooks of A5 format, and that there is a total of 55 such pieces. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You drafted this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you execute the handover of these documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you -- could we scroll down, please, to see the signatures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me now, what reasons didn't you produce an overview of the notebooks to be handed over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say that at this moment. I believe that it went for notebooks which were not particularly important. In the first handover case, we selected notebooks which were pertinent to a certain case. After that, ICTY representatives would subsequently take and grab whatever was in relation to that relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this is your explanation for why you did not produce such a table for the 55 notebooks now in question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really recall at this point. I think there should be a table or an overview or a list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see any such lists in the materials available to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution help? Is there any such list?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you referring specifically to the 55 A4 notebooks and the one A5?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm referring to what the witness supposes there should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have not come across one that was prepared per se by the witness. There is such a list, but it was not prepared by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic, go ahead, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have not received such a list. Maybe it does exist. It would be interesting to have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, was there anybody else apart from you who would prepare such lists?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mainly, I was in charge of such tasks. There were some other people. I believe that we prepared a list. Why it is not here, I don't know. Maybe it hasn't been taken over. Because it was one year later. We had already gained some experience in this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You signed this report on handover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that there is an indication that it was produced in three copies and that there were no schedules or annexes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to turn to a record dating back to 2000. This is also Prosecution Exhibit 1072. Were you present when the files were the archive stated here and were handed over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would taking a look at the signatures help you? Can we please scroll down to see the signatures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at annex 2, which is the list of the daily logs of the station containing information on electronic reconnaissance. Can we turn to page 2? Because this is annex 1. We need to take a look at annex 2. That would be the next page. That's it. Was this list drafted in the same way as the earlier one; that in one column we have the number of the station's daily log, and then the last column the dates of the period which these daily logs covered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at number 4, according to which this station logbook was opened on the 28th of May 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that in fact it was first used on the 13th of April, and that its ending date was actually 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there occurred errors in the transcription.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see there that the station's daily log was entered into the record on the 24th of April 1995; but that in fact, it was first used on the 10th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then look at number 6, which doesn't bear a date at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at number 10, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, could I interrupt for one minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we have a translation issue, because we've switched translators. I may be wrong, but we are switching from the term notebook to logbook. And there can be a very significant difference between the two, and I just wanted to alert everyone to that. And it can get confusing. Because a logbook, in the context that we normally see it, is something where there is entries made, and it's a document that is kept by regulation many times, as opposed to these notebooks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I appreciate what you are saying, but yesterday one simple direct unequivocal question was put to the witness; whether one -- whether we ought to distinguish between logbooks and notebooks, and he said that they are one and the same thing. So I think you need to explain yourself somewhat better in order that we can understand exact your preoccupation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can get you to the part of the transcript, yesterday's transcript. But again take my word for it that the question was put and answered in that manner using exactly the same words rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I recall that. What I think is happening, and I may be wrong, but I think the translations are using -- one is using logbook and one is using notebook. And I think that's the only difference, and my point is so that in this context of this witness, is they are the same thing. But if we do start talking about logbooks, which could come up at any time because there are military logbooks that are associated with this record keeping, then we are going to get very confused. And I just want to alert people to it. I don't know exactly what's happening, because I don't understand the language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't think we ought to discuss any further in the presence of the witness. But the witness has heard what you had to say, Mr. McCloskey. I haven't given the word -- the floor to Mr. Zivanovic, if he wishes to respond to that. But then I will come back to you, Witness, to hear what you have to say about what is alleged to be or what is being submitted to be a possible source of confusion. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me put a question to the witness, and that will clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In view of these questions, or rather, the questions that I put to you, do they actually relate to the notebooks that we discussed earlier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "mostly yes," does it mean that among the documents that I quoted to you now, there are documents that are not notebooks of intercepts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a heap of material. There were around 50 notebooks, and then different forms that had cover pages and that we would use as notebooks. The purpose to which these documents were put was the same, regardless of whether they were called stanicni dnevnik, station logbook or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was interpreted as "station logbook or something else." I believe you said or "sveska," notebook. All of them, in fact, contained intercepted conversations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please look at number 10 now? Was this notebook entered into the record on the 28th of April, and was it first used on the 4th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at number 11. Was it first used 27th of March and, in fact, was put to use earlier on the 8th of March?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Mr. Zivanovic, please do appreciate that the interpreters spend an hour and a half in that restricted space, trying to catch up with a barrage of evidence that is most often or very frequently overlapping. It's very difficult for them; and if you don't cooperate, what we get is half-baked meals, you know. I mean, the interpretation or the transcript will not reflect completely what is being testified. So, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will bear that in mind. I apologise to you and the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at number 14 -- no -- yes, number 14. Does it bear the date of opening the notebook on the 7th of April, and it was first put to use on the 14th of March?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I can explain this. We found notebooks; and whichever we could get hold of, we would use as notebooks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You've already explained this to us, thank you. There is quite a few of such notebooks, and whoever wishes to find them will be able to. They are in evidence. We've discussed this -- is there something else here? You said that the encryption department kept their own records. Were these records in fact stored?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The encryption department had a notebook containing telegrams that were incoming and those that were outgoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Were these notebooks handed over to the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall at this time, but I believe that the entire documentation was handed over to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, please, you overlapped. Please try to allow a pause. Don't jump straight in with your answer, even before Mr. Zivanovic has finished his question. Allow a short interval of time, a pause, a brief pause. But it is necessary. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw this working map here. You said that you made it pursuant to the request by the ICTY representatives, and that you produced it as per the state of affairs in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an original working map in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hand it over to the ICTY representatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please look at another annex? And the number it bears is 0204-0772.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, both Judge Kwon and myself and Judge Prost have found it's not in the system, or at least the number you gave us 0204-0772.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the outset, I said that a number of these documents have not been uploaded into e-court, and that we ought to use other technical equipment to show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Technical help, advice required. What can we do? Is it available? Is the witness seeing it? Okay. But we need to see it, too. Do we have a hard copy of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I have a nod from the Prosecution side, which indicates that they do have a hard copy. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understand we have a hard copy of -- well, we have the original. I don't know if that would be useful in terms of displaying that to the witness or for counsel's purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it a single-page document or a multiple-page document? What is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are several pages there, but one would suffice, just as an exemplary. Can we show the witness 0204-0834 in that case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it the right page?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I'm grateful to the Prosecution team. We can put it on the ELMO, please, and no broadcast unless we authorise it. We had better focus.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see the date of the report under which date it was sent? Is it the 11th of February?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-131 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the heading of the report says.
